title: Optimizing Lambda Performance
content:
Advanced Lambda Performance Optimization with Provisioned Concurrency Overall In this lab, you’ll learn the basics and practice of Advanced Lambda Performance Optimization with Provisioned Concurrency. Perform creating public and private instance connections.
Content Introduction Preparation Create and configure Lambda function Configure API Gateway Set Auto Scaling for Provisioned Concurrency Clean up resources

title: Introduction
content:
AWS Lambda is a serverless computing service provided by Amazon Web Services that allows you to run code without managing servers. You just need to write code and deploy, while AWS automatically handles infrastructure, scaling, and maintenance.
Key features:
No need to manage servers: No need to configure, operate, or update operating systems. Automatic scaling: Lambda automatically scales according to the number of actual requests. Pay as you go: You only pay for execution time and function calls, no charge when not in use. Supports many languages: Node.js, Python, Java, Go, .NET, Ruby, and more. Deep integration with AWS services: Can be triggered from S3, API Gateway, DynamoDB, CloudWatch, EventBridge, and more. Popular applications:
Process images, videos, files immediately upon upload to S3. Automatically respond to API or webhook events. Automatically backup and synchronize data. Build microservices or simple backends.

title: Preparation
content:
You need to create an activated AWS account to perform this lab.
AWS account activated. Install AWS CLI. https://docs.aws.amazon.com/cli/latest/userguide/getting-started-install.html Or run command in cmd: msiexec.exe /i https://awscli.amazonaws.com/AWSCLIV2.msi Download the installer .msi file for Windows. Run the installation. After installation, close cmd, reopen cmd. Check if AWS CLI has been successfully installed by entering cmd: aws –version Created IAM role with permissions for Lambda, API Gateway, CloudWatch.

title: Set Auto Adjust for Provisioned Concurrency
content:
Open cmd. Run configure command.
After running configure we run aws application-autoscaling register-scalable-target –service-namespace lambda –resource-id function:lambda-performance-test:prod –scalable-dimension lambda:function:ProvisionedConcurrency –min-capacity 1 –max-capacity 5
So you’ve just registered a Scalable Goal for Provisioned Concurrency Enable Provisioned Concurrency.

title: Clean up resources
content: Delete Lambda Function & Alias. • Go to AWS Lambda => Functions => Select function lambda-performance-test. • Delete alias prod first, then delete the function. Delete API Gateway. Run this command in cmd: aws apigateway get -rest-api. Wish everyone a successful practice.
